name: The Last Emperors and the Thrones They Lost
description: The Qing, the Romanovs, the Ottomans, the Negus and the Shah: how ancient monarchies ended in war, revolution and exile between 1908 and 1979.

checkpoints.name: A dying dynasty
checkpoints.note: Empress Dowager Cixi held power at the Qing court for decades. Just before her death in 1908 she had the child Puyi named emperor, and the Xinhai Revolution ended the Qing dynasty in 1912, closing two thousand years of imperial rule in China.

checkpoints.name: Thrones lost in war
checkpoints.note: World War I toppled several monarchies. Nicholas II abdicated in 1917 and the Romanov dynasty ended; the Russian Revolution brought Lenin to power. In 1918 Wilhelm II fell in revolution and Austria-Hungary broke up, and the Ottoman sultanate ended in 1922 as Mustafa Kemal Ataturk founded a republic.

checkpoints.name: Puppets and exile
checkpoints.note: Puyi was made head of the Japanese-backed state of Manchukuo in 1932. In Ethiopia Haile Selassie, crowned in 1930, was driven out by the Italian invasion in 1936 and returned in 1941 with British help, ruling an empire that had a long history.

checkpoints.name: The last great thrones
checkpoints.note: Haile Selassie was deposed in 1974 and the Ethiopian monarchy ended soon after. In Iran the Pahlavi dynasty fell in the Iranian Revolution, with the Shah leaving in 1979 and Ayatollah Khomeini returning from exile to lead the new republic.
